You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the failing test does:
  - ExternalXMLNamespaceTest.testElementDOM calls doTestElement(DocumentContainer.MODEL_DOM).
  - doTestElement delegates to doTest("/ElementA/B:ElementB", model, "MY VALUE").
  - doTest creates a JXPathContext over a DocumentContainer for ExternalNS.xml, then registers two namespaces:
    - "A" -> "foo"
    - "B" -> "bar"
  - It then asserts that the XPath /ElementA/B:ElementB yields "MY VALUE".
- How the XML is parsed:
  - createDocumentContainer(String model) builds a DocumentContainer for ExternalNS.xml and explicitly sets namespace awareness to false (comment notes this only works for DOM).
- Relevant DOM handling for namespaced attributes/elements:
  - In the DOM model, prefixed names are treated specially when the parser is namespace-aware. With namespaceAware=false, DOM nodes typically lack namespace URIs; prefixes remain part of the nodeName, and the namespace URI/localName fields are null.
  - DOMNodePointer.createAttribute(JXPathContext, QName) shows how names with prefixes are resolved:
    - It extracts the prefix from the QName.
    - It calls getNamespaceURI(prefix) to find a namespace URI.
    - If no URI is found (ns == null), it throws JXPathException("Unknown namespace prefix: " + prefix).
    - Notably, this method ignores the passed JXPathContext when resolving the prefix.
- Where the mismatch occurs:
  - The test relies on namespaces being registered programmatically on the JXPathContext (A -> foo, B -> bar).
  - The DOM model here is namespace-unaware, so DOM nodes don’t expose namespace URIs. That makes any resolver that relies only on DOM-provided namespace information likely to return null for a prefix.
  - DOMNodePointer.createAttribute demonstrates the core problem: it uses getNamespaceURI(prefix) and throws if null, without consulting the registered namespaces on the JXPathContext. This is consistent with the issue report’s symptom: attributes with a namespace prefix (e.g., xsi) trigger “Unknown namespace prefix: …” even when the user expects to be able to register or otherwise resolve that prefix.
- How this causes the failure:
  - During XPath evaluation like /ElementA/B:ElementB (and similarly when creating attributes), the engine needs to resolve the prefix B to a namespace URI.
  - Because the DOM tree was parsed with namespace awareness disabled, and because the resolver used in DOMNodePointer does not fall back to the context’s registered namespaces, getNamespaceURI("B") returns null.
  - That leads either to a failure to match the element in selection, or to the explicit exception path for attributes seen in DOMNodePointer.createAttribute ("Unknown namespace prefix: B" or "xsi"), matching the reported problem.
- Conclusion:
  - The failure is due to incomplete namespace resolution in the DOM model: DOMNodePointer resolves prefixes only from the DOM node’s in-scope namespace declarations (or DOM API) and ignores the JXPathContext’s registered namespaces. With namespace-aware parsing disabled, and even in general when a prefix is only registered via the context, this yields null and an “Unknown namespace prefix” exception.
  - The fix should ensure that prefix resolution in the DOM model consults the JXPathContext’s registered namespaces (or scans xmlns attributes when namespace-aware=false) before deciding the prefix is unknown, rather than ignoring the context as createAttribute currently does.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
